name: Colli Berici

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Cabernet Sauvignon, Sangiovese, Grenache, Carignan and Zinfandel fully without cooking off their freshness.
Pinot Gris is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Merlot is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 2°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Big crops are possible, but quality tops out at acceptable.
